comments.author: @TheUnlistedWorld
comments.text: Most communities up there have no road in at all. Everything arrives by plane, or by barge in the few weeks the water's open, or by ice road that only exists while the ground stays frozen. A place you can drive to isn't the North most Canadians mean. Change my mind.

comments.author: @TravelDiscovery-q9q
comments.text: Really enjoyed this one! Canada’s vast North feels like a completely different world with  beautiful, remote, and fascinating to see.

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: I'm so glad you enjoyed the journey into such a unique and remote part of the world!

replies.author: @BestTravel2

comments.author: @AmazingDiscoveriesTopUS
comments.text: The most amazing part isn't that the Uros people built floating islands- it's that they keep rebuilding their home generation after generation.

comments.author: @chaselandtv
comments.text: I love how the documentary captures the two distinct Canadian personalities [04:41]: the cozy hibernation around hockey arenas in winter [14:38] versus the joyful outdoor energy the second summer arrives

replies.author: @trueunrealglobe
replies.text: Every time I watch this channel, my travel bucket list somehow becomes longer. There are clearly far more incredible places in the world than I realized.

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: That's awesome to hear! Canada truly is a special place, and I'm glad you enjoyed seeing a glimpse of it.

comments.author: @AdamsChloe-m3t
comments.text: Surviving at -40°C in total darkness for months requires a level of mental toughness most city dwellers can’t even fathom. Absolute respect for the northern spirit.

replies.author: @BestTravel2
replies.text: It truly is incredible what people endure and thrive in up north. The human spirit is remarkably resilient.

comments.author: @fabulouslife-mm
comments.text: As a Canadian, this documentary captured the essence of our daily life perfectly! The contrast between our quiet, cozy winters and the explosive energy of summer is so true. Incredible visuals and narration!

comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: What do you think would be the hardest part of living here: the weather, the distance, the cost of supplies, or the isolation?

replies.author: @BestHiddenPlaces
replies.text: For me, the isolation would be the hardest especially during long winters when roads close and supplies become limited.
